newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan policymakers plan ice-breaking China visit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan policymakers plan ice-breaking China visit.

text.p: Taipei's policymakers toward Beijing are planning a tour of China they hope will break the 19-month political impasse between the two diplomatic rivals, the state-run Central News Agency reported on Sunday.

Shi Hwei-you, vice-chairman of the cabinet-level Mainland Affairs Council, and Lee Ching-ping, deputy secretary-general of the semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation were expected to join a delegation to visit China in April, the agency said.
If he goes, Shi would become the most senior official from the council to visit China.
The group would meet Chinese officials to discuss potential problems in a previous agreement on cross-strait document authentication, the agency said.
A furious Beijing indefinitely suspended talks with Taiwan after President Lee Teng-hui's landmark private visit to the United States in mid 1995.

China, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since the island split from mainland China after a civil war in 1949, said Lee's U.S. visit showed he sought Taiwanese independence rather than reunification with the mainland.

Last year, Beijing rattled Taiwan with war games and missile tests in waters near the island during the run-up to the island's March 23 presidential election. Beijing acknowledged the scare tactics were aimed at intimidating Taiwan voters into abandoning independence.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin last week invited Taiwan's ruling and opposition parties to come up with constructive suggestions on ways to achieve reunification.
